content:
- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.7) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or trending downward (sentiment < 0.5) — model fails to capture mean reversion or bearish momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods — true values often dip below forecast before rebounding, especially in first 5–7 days.
- Model overreacts to recent highs — if last 3–5 prices are rising, forecast often peaks too early and then drops.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise — smooths out sharp corrections.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high for extended periods after strong upward moves — especially when sentiment is high but then drops.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates near-term volatility — true values show more downward correction than model suggests.
- If sentiment is consistently below 0.5 over 5+ days, model should reduce forecast slope — avoid upward bias.
- If sentiment is above 0.7 for 3+ days, model should reduce forecast peak — avoid overcorrection after spike.
